related.note: Both are about JFK asking CIA Director McCone for UFO information in 1963. This telling has it as a request for a full briefing on June 5, 1963, while the story has it as a letter dated November 12, 1963.

plain: Ten days before he was killed, President John F. Kennedy is said to have written to the head of the CIA asking for all its data on unexplained objects. The letter is dated November 12, 1963, and is addressed to CIA director John McCone. Jesse Michels says it came out through FOIA, a US law that lets anyone request government records, and he gives the year of release as 2006 at some times and 2005 at others. In his telling, Kennedy asks for "all the data on unknowns" so that the Americans could coordinate with the Soviets, and Michels places it after Kennedy had fired the earlier CIA chief, Allen Dulles. Michels also stresses that its origin is disputed, calling it a letter "of kind of controversial provenance" that should be checked. He credits the records researcher John Greenewald Jr. for it in some tellings. The UFO historian Richard Dolan describes the same memo as Kennedy directing the CIA to share UFO data with the Soviet Union. If it is real, a sitting president was trying to open UFO secrets to a rival power just before his death.
